step1_analysis.description: This circuit forms the active negative-resistance core of an LC voltage-controlled oscillator. The cross-coupled PMOS and NMOS pairs provide the transconductance required to overcome tank losses and sustain oscillation, while the bottom NMOS acts as a tail current source to set the bias current.

paper_reference.title: Large-Signal Analysis of MOS Varactors Gm LC VCOs in CMOS

oscillation_frequency.description: The fundamental frequency of the oscillator's output waveform.

sky130_expected.calculation: f = 1 / (2 * pi * sqrt(L * C)). Using an ideal tank with L=6.4nH and C=0.5pF to match the paper's target, f = 2.81 GHz.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Determined by the LC tank components added to the testbench to replicate the paper's operating frequency.

voltage_swing.description: Peak-to-peak differential voltage swing across the tank nodes (N0 and N1).

sky130_expected.reasoning: The swing is determined by the tail current and the equivalent parallel resistance of the tank, operating in the current-limited regime.

power_consumption.description: Total DC power consumed by the oscillator core from the supply.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Based on the tail current set by the BIAS voltage (0.8V) and the 1.8V supply.

dc_bias.description: The common-mode DC voltage at the tank nodes (N0 and N1).

sky130_expected.calculation: PMOS must supply half the tail current (97.5uA). 97.5uA = 0.5 * 50u * 10 * (Vsg - 0.42)^2 -> Vsg = 1.04V. V_N0 = VDD - Vsg = 1.8 - 1.04 = 0.76V.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Determined by the Vsg required for the cross-coupled PMOS pair to source the DC tail current.

step3_testbench.description: Transient analysis to measure the oscillation frequency, differential voltage swing, power consumption, and DC bias of the VCO core. An ideal LC tank is added to enable oscillation.
step3_testbench.spice:
* VCO Core Testbench
.lib "${SKY130_PDK}" tt

.param W_xm1=5u L_xm1=0.5u
.param W_xm2=5u L_xm2=0.5u
.param W_xm3=5u L_xm3=0.5u
.param W_xm4=5u L_xm4=0.5u
.param W_xm5=5u L_xm5=0.5u

* Power and Bias Sources
VVDD VDD 0 1.8
VBIAS BIAS 0 0.8

* DUT: VCO Core
XM1 N1 N0 VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xm1} w={W_xm1}
XM2 N1 N0 N2 GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm2} w={W_xm2}
XM3 N0 N1 VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xm3} w={W_xm3}
XM4 N2 BIAS GND GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm4} w={W_xm4}
XM5 N0 N1 N2 GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm5} w={W_xm5}

* Ideal LC Tank (Tuned to ~2.8 GHz)
L1 N0 N1 6.4nH
C1 N0 N1 0.5pF
R1 N0 N1 5k

* Dependent source to easily measure differential voltage
B1 diff 0 V=v(N0)-v(N1)

* Initial condition to kickstart oscillation
.ic v(N0)=1.8 v(N1)=0.0

.control
* Run transient analysis
tran 10p 50n

* Measure Oscillation Frequency (using 10th to 11th zero-crossing to ensure steady state)
meas tran t1 trig v(diff) val=0 rise=10 targ v(diff) val=0 rise=11
let freq = 1/t1
print freq

* Measure Peak-to-Peak Voltage Swing
meas tran vmax max v(diff) from=30n to=50n
meas tran vmin min v(diff) from=30n to=50n
let swing = vmax - vmin
print swing

* Measure Power Consumption
meas tran id_avg avg i(VVDD) from=30n to=50n
let power = -id_avg * 1.8
print power

* Measure DC Bias Voltage at Tank
meas tran vdc_n0 avg v(N0) from=30n to=50n
print vdc_n0

quit
.endc
